A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ternary oxide phases Li 2 ZO 3, where Z = Al, Sc, In, and Ga, are Li ion conductive, and that the Li ion conductivities of Li 2 AlO 3 and Li 2 ScO 3 are comparable to that of LiAlO 2.
the Li ion conductivity of these phases is low, but that the Li loss during dc conductivity measurements is even lower, so that they are promising for use in solid-state batteries.

there is a small but growing number of Li ion conductors which have a high melting point, a low activation energy for conduction, a high chemical stability in air, and are thermodynamically stable with Li.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ternary oxide phases are not as stable against Li as was previously thought, and that the stability of these phases may be limited to temperatures below 400 K.
the ternary oxides are not good Li ion conductors, and the conductivity is not sufficient to be of use in an all solid state Li ion battery.
there are a number of phases that have been identified as Li ion conductors which may be thermally stable against Li loss at the anode.
